reason: 'confluent with each other / at the base' says that like parts (sori, segments, appendages) run together into one; FLOPO connate is the one-word quality for like parts that are joined, and PATO:0002512 'confluent with' is its relational form that needs a second part.

'costa strong', 'vein strong', 'pedicel strong' mean well developed and sturdy, which is PATO robust ('strong, thick or sturdy'); PATO:0001716 non-fragile, which lists 'strong' as a RELATED synonym, means resistance to breaking.

label: margined
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a distinct marginal band that differs from the rest of it in colour, texture, thickness or cell form. NOTE: Covers narrowly margined seeds and bracts and the bordered (limbidiate) leaves of mosses; the band itself is a plant organ margin (PO:0025005).
reason: 'Seed narrowly margined', 'bract with white-hyaline margin' describe a rim that differs from the body; no PATO or FLOPO term covers this, and the margin alone (PO:0025005) is present in every organ.
Delicate plants, awns and petals are slender and thin, so they are easily damaged; this matches PATO fragile, the opposite of the 'tough' rule below.

In botany, 'pungent' on a leaf, bract or apex means ending in a sharp, stiff point (FLOPO spine-tipped); with smell or odour it means a sharp odour (FLOPO spicy-scented, defined as a pungent, spicy odour). Bare 'fruit pungent' (taste) fits neither and stays unannotated.

label: appendiculate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's bearing one or more small outgrowths or appendages. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991029 horned and FLOPO:0991196 crested; the appendages of anthers, petals and peristome cilia have different origins, so no part is named.

'Margin stoutly bordered', 'peristome teeth bordered with a hyaline band', 'seed not bordered' mean the same as margined; 'not bordered' is its negation.
FLOPO reticulate already has 'net-veined' as an EXACT synonym and covers veins of leaves, sepals and fruits.

A hyphenated pair of shapes is a continuum between two values, as in 'linear-lanceolate'; PATO has lance-ovate and lanceolate-triangular but no ovate-triangular, and a pattern is better than a new term.

label: flat-topped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's upper surface or outline being more or less level, its distal parts reaching about the same height. NOTE: PATO:0002455 corymb-like is the inflorescence architecture; flat-topped cymes, panicles, fruits and moss lamella cells are not corymbs.
reason: Used for inflorescences, fruits, stems and cells. Corymb-like fits only the inflorescences and only by architecture, and truncated (PATO_0000936) is about an end that is cut off.

label: homogamous
definition: A structural quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of all its flowers being of the same sexual kind. NOTE: Opposite of FLOPO:0991178 heterogamous. The pollination sense (anthers and stigmas maturing together, 'flowers homogamous') is a different quality and is not covered.
reason: Standard term for Asteraceae capitula and grass spikelet pairs; it is the sibling of heterogamous, which the previous review added.
Hirsutulous = minutely hirsute; mapped to the broader value, as lobulate → lobed and prominulous → prominent in the previous review.
PATO non-fragile ('withstand great strain without tearing or breaking') has 'tough' as a RELATED synonym; this is the sense of tough leaf blades, rinds and rootstocks.
The pipeline maps 'ciliate' to PATO ciliated (e.g. leaf margin ciliated, FLOPO_0993395); eciliate is its negation, usually of a margin.

label: turgid
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being swollen and full, rounded in section rather than flattened, as if filled with fluid. NOTE: Not PATO:0001851 swollen or PATO:0001602 distended (abnormal), PATO:0002376 inflated (air-filled) or PATO:0001622 increased turgor (cell pressure).
reason: Turgid achenes, perigynia and seeds are plump in normal development; every nearby PATO term is either abnormal enlargement, air-filled, or cell pressure.

label: callose
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's bearing hard, thickened, often pale spots or tips (calluses). NOTE: Not the polysaccharide callose; 'callus' was rejected as a generic part, so this cannot be a presence rule.

A bulging midrib, vein or cell stands out from the surface; the previous review mapped protuberant and elevated to PATO prominent.
